prompt.adult: 1 Kings 16:21 says the people of Israel were divided into two parts. After “half of the people followed,” whom does the verse first name?
prompt.child: Israel split between two men. After “half of the people followed,” whom does 16:21 first name?
prompt.teen: 1 Kings 16:21: “half of the people followed” whom first?
prompt.older: According to 1 Kings 16:21, after “half of the people followed,” whom is first named?

verses.text: Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri.

explanation.child: Look right after “half of the people followed” in verse 21.
explanation.teen: 16:21 first names this man, then says half followed Omri. Read that name.
explanation.older: It follows “half of the people followed” in 16:21.

teaching.takeaway: Half followed Tibni the son of Ginath.

prompt.adult: 1 Kings 16:8 names Elah the son of Baasha. In 16:24, after Omri bought it from Shemer, for how much did he buy it?
prompt.child: Omri bought a place from Shemer. After naming Shemer, for how much does 16:24 say he bought it?
prompt.older: Read with 16:8, for how much does 16:24 say Omri bought it?

verses.text: And he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver; then he built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, Samaria, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah the son of Baasha became king over Israel, and reigned two years in Tirzah.

explanation.child: Look right after “from Shemer for” in verse 24.
explanation.teen: 16:8 names Elah; 16:24 names the price he paid. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:24 also says he “called the name of the city which he built, Samaria, after the name of Shemer.” 16:8 names Elah the son of Baasha.
teaching.takeaway: He bought it for two talents of silver.

prompt.adult: 1 Kings 16:10 names Zimri’s strike against Elah. In 16:23, in what year of Asa did Omri become king over Israel?
prompt.child: Omri became king over Israel in a year of King Asa. Which year does 16:23 name?
prompt.teen: 1 Kings 16:23: in what year of Asa did Omri become king?
prompt.older: Read with 16:10, in what year of Asa does 16:23 say Omri became king over Israel?

verses.text: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel, and reigned twelve years. Six years he reigned in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and struck him and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.

explanation.child: Look right after “In the” at the start of verse 23.
explanation.teen: 16:10 names Zimri’s strike; 16:23 opens with this date. Read that phrase.
explanation.older: It follows “In the” at the start of 16:23.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:23 also says Omri “reigned twelve years.” 16:10 says Zimri “reigned in his place.”
teaching.takeaway: Omri became king in the thirty-first year of Asa.

prompt.adult: 2 Kings 13:10 names Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz. In 15:13, after naming Shallum the son of Jabesh and the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah, how long was his time there?
prompt.child: Shallum’s time is measured in 15:13. After naming the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah, how long does the verse say it was?
prompt.teen: 2 Kings 15:13: after naming Uzziah, how long does it say his time was?
prompt.older: Read with 13:10, how long does 15:13 say Shallum’s time was?

verses.text: Shallum the son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned sixteen years.

explanation.child: Look just before “in Samaria” in verse 13.
explanation.teen: 13:10 names Jehoash; 15:13 ends with Shallum’s time. Read that phrase.
explanation.older: It comes just before “in Samaria” at the end of 15:13.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:13 begins, “Shallum the son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah.” 13:10 says Jehoash “reigned sixteen years.”
teaching.takeaway: He reigned a full month in Samaria.

For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, came to Samaria, and struck Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him; and he reigned in his place.

explanation.older: It follows the fiftieth year of Azariah in 15:23.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:23 also says he “reigned two years.” 15:14 says he struck Shallum in Samaria and killed him.
teaching.takeaway: Pekahiah the son of Menahem became king.

prompt.adult: 2 Chronicles 26:5 says Uzziah sought God while Zechariah lived. In 26:9, after “And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at,” what gate does the verse name first?
prompt.child: Uzziah built towers at named gates of Jerusalem. After “built towers in Jerusalem at,” what gate does 26:9 name first?

prompt.older: Read with 26:5, what gate does 26:9 name first?

verses.text: And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the corner buttress of the wall; then he fortified them.
He sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.

explanation.child: Look right after “built towers in Jerusalem at” in verse 9.
explanation.teen: 26:5 names Zechariah; 26:9 first names this gate. Read that name.
explanation.older: It follows “built towers in Jerusalem at” in 26:9.

teaching.extended_explanation: 26:9 also names the Valley Gate and a buttress of the wall. 26:5 says, “and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.”
teaching.takeaway: He first built at the Corner Gate.

prompt.adult: 2 Chronicles 27:4 says Jotham built cities in the mountains of Judah. In 26:15, after “And he made devices in Jerusalem,” how does the verse say they were invented?
prompt.child: Uzziah made devices in Jerusalem. After “And he made devices in Jerusalem,” how does 26:15 say they were invented?
prompt.teen: 2 Chronicles 26:15: “And he made devices in Jerusalem,” how invented?
prompt.older: Read with 27:4, how does 26:15 say the devices were invented?

verses.text: And he made devices in Jerusalem, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. So his fame spread far and wide, for he was marvelously helped till he became strong.
Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.

explanation.child: Look right after “devices in Jerusalem,” in verse 15.
explanation.teen: 27:4 names Jotham’s building; 26:15 names how these devices were invented. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 26:15 also says they were “to shoot arrows and large stones.” 27:4 also says, “and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.”
teaching.takeaway: They were invented by skillful men.

prompt.adult: 2 Chronicles 27:8 says Jotham was twenty-five when he became king. In 27:6, after “So Jotham became mighty, because,” why did he become mighty?
prompt.child: The verse tells why Jotham became mighty. After “because,” what does 27:6 say?
prompt.teen: 2 Chronicles 27:6: “So Jotham became mighty, because” why?
prompt.older: Read with 27:8, why does 27:6 say Jotham became mighty?

verses.text: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD his God.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

explanation.teen: 27:8 names his length of rule; 27:6 names why he became mighty. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 27:6 also says this was “before the LORD his God.” 27:8 also names his length of rule in Jerusalem.
teaching.takeaway: He became mighty because he prepared his ways.
